player_0.content: New plan: I failed because I assigned high scores to emotions like "Superior" and "Anxious" based on the surface-level aggression of the dialogue, ignoring the underlying context of professional rivalry and mutual frustration. The characters are entrenched in a stalemate where both feel the other is incompetent and out of touch, leading to a shared sense of futility rather than one-sided dominance or anxiety. Next time, I will prioritize "Disappointed" as the primary emotion (score 9-10) because the dialogue explicitly highlights the failure of their experience and modern methods to solve the case ("experience isn't everything," "stuck on the same case"). I will assign a low score to "Superior" (0-1) since both characters are attacking each other's competence, negating any sense of superiority, and keep "Anxious" low (1-2) as the tone is confrontational and resigned rather than fearful.
